abstract: Most membrane and secreted proteins undergo glycosylation, the covalent posttranslational addition of oligosaccharide chains. Glycans, which constitute up to 30\% of a glycoprotein's mass, alter protein trafficking, dynamics, interactions, and thus function. Because of their heterogeneity, rapid dynamics, and conformational richness, glycans are difficult to characterise experimentally, so molecular simulations can provide a powerful alternative for studying their effects on proteins. Given that the time and length scales involved are typically large, coarse-grained models can be used to enhance the sampling and allow for the study of interactions of glycoproteins in their cellular context. Although individual saccharides and glycans have been parameterised for coarse-grained simulations, modelling new glycan structures has largely required system-specific parameter development, and no general framework connects transferable glycan models with automated construction of complete glycoproteins. Here, we introduce GlycoMarinate, a general framework for coarse-grained modelling of N-glycoproteins within the Martini 3 force field. The framework supports two complementary levels of glycan description: a transferable generic model designed for broad applicability, and refined glycan-specific models optimised against atomistic conformational ensembles. We derive and validate refined models for ten representative high-mannose, hybrid, and complex N-glycans. Both descriptions are integrated into an automated workflow that generates the topologies and clash-free starting coordinates for site-specifically glycosylated proteins. We demonstrate the framework on biologically relevant systems, including the densely glycosylated SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.
